identity.title: HINTS (head impulse, nystagmus, test of skew) — ACUTE VESTIBULAR SYNDROME ONLY; validated by neuro-ophthalmologists

technique.how: Only in acute vestibular syndrome (continuous vertigo with spontaneous nystagmus). Three steps: (1) horizontal head impulse test; (2) nystagmus in primary and eccentric gaze, looking for direction change; (3) alternate cover test for vertical skew. Dangerous HINTS = normal head impulse OR direction-changing nystagmus OR skew; benign = abnormal HIT, unidirectional nystagmus, no skew.
technique.prerequisites: Spontaneous nystagmus must be present; examiner trained in eliciting catch-up saccades and skew. Add bedside hearing (HINTS+): new unilateral hearing loss counts as dangerous.
technique.contraindications: Cervical instability/dissection for the impulse component; patient unable to fixate or cooperate.

interpretation.positive_finding: Any dangerous component indicates a central cause: pooled sensitivity 93-97% and specificity 83-98% depending on examiner group; in the original neuro-ophthalmologist study 100% sensitive, 96% specific (LR+ 25, LR- 0.00), outperforming early MRI-DWI.
interpretation.negative_finding: A fully benign HINTS in AVS performed by a trained examiner makes stroke unlikely (pooled LR- about 0.09); however when applied by emergency physicians without specific training, pooled specificity was only 44% with sensitivity 83%, so a benign result is far less reliable.
interpretation.pitfalls: Applied outside AVS (no nystagmus, episodic vertigo, BPPV) it is invalid and produces false 'dangerous' results (normal HIT is normal in a healthy person). AICA strokes with labyrinthine infarction give an abnormal HIT (benign-looking) - add hearing (HINTS+). Skew and subtle saccades are easily missed by non-experts.
interpretation.changes_what: Dangerous HINTS in AVS: stroke pathway/MRI even if CT normal. Benign HINTS by trained examiner: supports neuritis; by untrained examiner do not use to withhold imaging.

estimates.target_condition: Central lesion (stroke, hemorrhage, other) in acute vestibular syndrome - dangerous HINTS
estimates.population: 101 consecutive high-risk AVS patients (25 peripheral, 76 central); examined by a single neuro-ophthalmologist/neuro-otologist
estimates.reference_standard: MRI (or CT) for stroke; normal MRI plus clinical follow-up for peripheral
estimates.quote: a dangerous H.I.N.T.S. result was 100% sensitive and 96% specific ... giving a positive likelihood ratio of 25 (95%CI 3.66-170.59)

estimates.target_condition: Vertebrobasilar stroke in AVS - HINTS performed by neurologists (fellowship-trained neuro-otology/vascular neurology)
estimates.population: Pooled prospective ED AVS studies (subset of 5 studies, 617 participants) with neurologist examiners
estimates.quote: The HINTS examination, when performed by neurologists, had a sensitivity of 96.7% (95% CI = 93.1% to 98.5%, I2 = 0%) and specificity of 94.8%

estimates.target_condition: Vertebrobasilar stroke in AVS - HINTS performed by a mixed cohort of board-certified emergency physicians and neurologists
estimates.population: Pooled ED AVS studies where examiners included emergency physicians (Ohle meta-analysis)
estimates.quote: the sensitivity was 83% (95% CI = 63% to 95%) and specificity was 44% (95% CI = 36% to 51%)

estimates.population: Subspecialist-examined subgroup of 10 pooled AVS cohorts (n=800 total)
estimates.reference_standard: Delayed MRI-DWI for peripheral cases; confirmatory neuroimaging for stroke
estimates.quote: higher specificity for the subspecialist group vs. the non-subspecialist group (97.6% [94.9-100.0] vs. 89.1% [83.0-95.2], p=0.007)
estimates.location: Results, 'Diagnostic accuracy of bedside examination findings', Figure 4 and supplementary Table 3 (Ann Neurol 2023;94:295; PMC10524166)

estimates.target_condition: Central AVS - HINTS by non-subspecialists (other training backgrounds, instructed in test performance)
estimates.population: Non-subspecialist-examined subgroup of 10 pooled AVS cohorts
estimates.reference_standard: Delayed MRI-DWI for peripheral cases; confirmatory neuroimaging for stroke
estimates.quote: sensitivity values were very similar and not statistically different (94.3% [88.2-100.0] vs. 95.0% [91.2-98.9], p=0.55)
estimates.location: Results, 'Diagnostic accuracy of bedside examination findings', Figure 4 and supplementary Table 3 (Ann Neurol 2023;94:295; PMC10524166)

estimates.population: 10 pooled AVS cohorts, n=800 (422 central, 378 peripheral)
estimates.reference_standard: Delayed MRI-DWI for peripheral cases; confirmatory neuroimaging for stroke
estimates.location: Results, 'Diagnostic accuracy of bedside examination findings', Figure 3 (Ann Neurol 2023;94:295; PMC10524166)

estimates.target_condition: Posterior circulation stroke (any stroke) in AVS - positive HINTS
estimates.population: 6 studies, 644 AVS patients, 200 with acute stroke; MRI-confirmed
estimates.quote: For any stroke, the pooled sensitivity was 95.5% (95% CI: 92.6-98.4%) and specificity was 71.2% (95% CI: 67.0-75.4%).

estimates.target_condition: Central cause of acute vertigo/dizziness - HINTS (all examiners, ED population)
estimates.population: ED patients with acute vertigo or dizziness; 14 studies, 1781 patients
estimates.quote: HINTS (head impulse, nystagmus, test of skew)-14 studies, 1781 patients, sensitivity 92.9% (95% CI 79.1%-97.9%, high) and specificity 83.4% (95% CI 69.6%-91.7%

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Only for acute vestibular syndrome with spontaneous nystagmus; not for episodic, positional or resolved vertigo, patients without nystagmus, or those who cannot fixate. Do not withhold imaging on a benign HINTS obtained by an untrained examiner.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Any dangerous component, new unilateral hearing loss, or inability to stand mandates stroke work-up; MRI-DWI within 48 h is falsely negative in about 15% of posterior strokes, so a negative early MRI does not override dangerous HINTS.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Performance is examiner-dependent: specificity 97.6% (subspecialists) vs 89.1% (trained non-subspecialists, Ann Neurol 2023) and only 44% in a mixed emergency-physician cohort (Ohle 2020); individual-study HINTS sensitivity ranges 78-99%, specificity 78-99%.

extraction_notes: SCOPE: all estimates apply only to acute vestibular syndrome (continuous vertigo with spontaneous nystagmus), except the GRACE-3 estimate which pools a broader ED vertigo/dizziness population and is kept separate. Estimates are split by examiner expertise and never averaged: Kattah 2009 (single neuro-ophthalmologist; PMC full text, Results and Table 4), Ohle 2020 (neurologists vs mixed emergency-physician cohort; abstract), Ann Neurol 2023 (subspecialist vs non-subspecialist; PMC full text, Results; SROC values in Figure 4/supplementary Table 3), Krishnan 2019 (all examiners, MRI standard; abstract). Kattah NLR CI (0.00-0.11) taken from Table 1 'subtle oculomotor signs' row, which is the HINTS composite; Table 4 gives 0.00 (0.00-0.12) for ischemic stroke only. Tarnutzer 2011 CMAJ anchor cited without numbers (abstract-only PMC deposit).
